In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that vitamin D may play in cancer risk.
the role of vitamin D and calcium in cancer prevention.
the role of vitamin D, UVB, and calcium in reducing the risk for cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vitamin D deficiency is associated with a higher risk of cancer, but it is not yet clear whether vitamin D sufficiency is associated with lower cancer risk.
vitamin D deficiency and insufficiency are associated with increased cancer risk and mortality.
vitamin D and calcium supplementation may be beneficial in the prevention of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IARC report was not balanced and did not accurately reflect the current state of the science.
vitamin D and calcium supplementation reduces cancer risk, especially in postmenopusal women.
vitamin D deficiency is a major cause of chronic diseases including cancer and vitamin D supplementation should be recommended to prevent cancer and other chronic diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin D is a critical factor that can be manipulated by public health policy.
there is no doubt that vitamin D has important roles in health, and that vitamin D status should be optimized to reduce the risk of cancer and other diseases.
